content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To get a new camera, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Read professional reviews of the top three contenders (2 hours)
Step 2. Transfer funds from savings to checking account (1 day)
Step 3. Create a spreadsheet of desired technical specifications (1 hour)
Step 4. Print out the final purchase receipt for your records (2 minutes)
Step 5. Compare ISO performance across different sensor sizes (3 hours)
Step 6. Check local store inventory for the chosen model (15 minutes)
Step 7. Watch YouTube field tests of the autofocus system (45 minutes)
Step 8. Calculate the total budget including taxes and accessories (30 minutes)
Step 9. Decide between a mirrorless or DSLR system (1 day)
Step 10. Visit a showroom to hold the camera in person (2 hours)
Step 11. Read user forums regarding long-term reliability (4 hours)
Step 12. Choose the best lens kit for the camera body (1 hour)
Step 13. Drive to the electronics store (30 minutes)
Step 14. Purchase a high-speed UHS-II memory card (10 minutes)
Step 15. Research compatible external flash units (1 hour)
Step 16. Sell your old camera gear to increase your budget (3 days)
Step 17. Subscribe to photography newsletters for discount codes (5 minutes)
Step 18. Determine if full-frame or APS-C is necessary (2 hours)
Step 19. Identify the primary genre of photography you will pursue (2 days)
Step 20. Look for seasonal promotional bundles (1 hour)
Step 21. Withdraw cash for a small-store discount (20 minutes)
Step 22. Download the camera’s digital manual to preview features (30 minutes)
Step 23. Research the best camera bags for travel (1 hour)
Step 24. Buy a protective screen cover (5 minutes)
Step 25. Ask a professional photographer for a recommendation (1 hour)
Step 26. Check the manufacturer's website for firmware updates (20 minutes)
Step 27. Complete the final transaction at the register (10 minutes)
Step 28. Evaluate the video recording capabilities (2 hours)
Step 29. Finalize the decision on the specific color and finish (10 minutes)
Step 30. Clean up your old gear for listing online (1 hour)
Step 31. Order a comfortable neck strap (15 minutes)
Step 32. Browse a wide selection of third-party accessories (2 hours)
Step 33. Set aside money for a photography workshop (1 week)
Step 34. Select a sturdy tripod (45 minutes)
Step 35. Verify the warranty terms and return policy (30 minutes)
Step 36. Compare prices between five different online retailers (2 hours)
Step 37. Set a maximum price limit for the purchase (30 minutes)
Step 38. Organize your new camera bag (15 minutes)
Step 39. Locate a nearby authorized dealer (10 minutes)
Step 40. Define your specific photographic needs (1 day)
Step 41. Read about the battery life and spare battery costs (1 hour)
Step 42. Consult a "Best Cameras of the Year" buying guide (1 hour)
Step 43. Decide which focal lengths are most important (2 hours)
Step 44. Pick a specialized cleaning kit for the sensor (10 minutes)
Step 45. Determine if you need an extended protection plan (30 minutes)
Step 46. Check your driver's license for store identification (1 minute)
Step 47. Purchase a spare rechargeable battery (5 minutes)
Step 48. Review your monthly expenses to find extra savings (3 hours)
Step 49. Sign up for a 1-year accidental damage insurance policy (20 minutes)
Step 50. Look for manufacturer rebates and mail-in offers (1 hour)
